# FSx for ONTAP Cyber Resilience Patterns

> Multi-layered cyber resilience reference patterns for Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, deployed as
> CloudFormation on AWS. It combines storage-native security (Autonomous Ransomware Protection,
> FPolicy, SnapLock, Tamperproof Snapshot, Multi-Admin Verification), file scanning with TrendAI
> Vision One File Security and Deep Instinct for NetApp ONTAP, and event-driven automated response
> (FPolicy to Amazon EventBridge to AWS Step Functions), with Snapshot, SnapMirror and FlexClone for
> recovery. The documentation describes how each control works, its trade-offs, and what is
> irreversible; it never instructs enabling a WORM or retention feature on its own.

## How to read this repository

The README is the primary hub (English at the repository root `README.md`; the Japanese hub is at
`docs/ja/README.md`). The repository compares several security technologies, and every comparison
states trade-offs symmetrically and includes a "how to choose" section rather than ranking vendors.

Safety note: SnapLock and other WORM/retention features make data undeletable for a retention period
and are irreversible — the file system can stay undeletable until the period expires, even for
administrators. This repository documents these features but does not enable them, and the
CloudFormation template that would create locked storage is intentionally not offered as a one-step
deploy. A reader must make an explicit retention decision before enabling any such feature.

- [README (English)](README.md): Primary hub. Overview, get-started table, architecture, constraints.
- [README (Japanese)](docs/ja/README.md): Japanese hub, same structure.

## Architecture

- [Architecture Overview](docs/architecture/overview.md): The security layers, how detection flows into event-driven response, and what each layer is responsible for.
- [Companion Repository Integration Guide](docs/en/companion-repos-integration.md): How this repository's patterns relate to the adoption, observability, S3 Access Points and RAG repositories.
- [Cyber Resilience Framework Mapping](docs/en/cyber-resilience-framework-mapping.md): The only CSF 2.0 mapping in this repository, including exfiltration, management-plane compromise and the storage-layer boundary.
- [Cyber Resilience Framework Mapping (JA)](docs/ja/cyber-resilience-framework-mapping.md): Japanese counterpart with the same sections.

## Storage-native security (ONTAP)

- [ARP (Autonomous Ransomware Protection) Configuration](docs/ontap-native/arp-configuration.md): Configuring ONTAP's on-box ransomware detection and how its alerts feed the response pipeline.
- [ARP Active-Mode Behaviour: Measurement Plan](docs/ontap-native/arp-active-mode-measurement-plan.md): The plan for measuring ARP active-mode behaviour, with the environment to be stated alongside any result.
- [FPolicy Configuration](docs/ontap-native/fpolicy-configuration.md): Configuring FPolicy so file events can drive automated response.
- [Multi-Admin Verification (MAV) Configuration](docs/ontap-native/mav-configuration.md): Requiring multiple administrators to approve privileged operations, limiting the blast radius of a compromised admin.
- [fsxadmin Permissions & Limitations](docs/ontap-native/fsxadmin-limitations.md): What the fsxadmin role can and cannot do on FSx for ONTAP, and where management-plane limits affect these patterns.
- [SnapLock Configuration](docs/ontap-native/snaplock-configuration.md): Reference for ONTAP SnapLock WORM behaviour and its irreversibility. Describes the feature; it is not a deploy step, and enabling WORM requires an explicit retention decision.
- [Tamperproof Snapshot Configuration](docs/ontap-native/tamperproof-snapshot.md): Snapshot locking that prevents deletion of recovery points until a retention period expires, including by administrators. Reference reading; prerequisites and licensing depend on your ONTAP and FSx for ONTAP version and should be checked against current AWS documentation.

## File scanning and AI prevention

- [TrendAI File Security — Vscan/ICAP Architecture](docs/trendai-file-security/architecture-vscan.md): Real-time malware scanning of file access via ONTAP Vscan over ICAP.
- [TrendAI File Security — S3 Access Points Batch Scan Architecture](docs/trendai-file-security/architecture-s3ap.md): Batch scanning of data reached through FSx for ONTAP S3 Access Points.
- [Deep Instinct for NetApp ONTAP — Architecture](docs/deep-instinct/architecture.md): AI-based zero-day threat prevention integrated with ONTAP.
- [Security Layer Comparison](docs/comparison-security-layers.md): ONTAP ARP, TrendAI File Security and Deep Instinct compared with symmetric trade-offs and a how-to-choose section.

## Observability

- [Security Monitoring Design](docs/observability/security-monitoring-design.md): Security metrics and Amazon CloudWatch dashboard design for these patterns.

## Data protection

- [AWS Backup Logically Air-Gapped Vault for Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP](docs/data-protection/aws-backup-logically-air-gapped-vault.md): Prerequisites, restore, and how to choose among SnapLock, tamperproof snapshots, cross-account SnapMirror/SnapVault and the vault. Documentation only, not tried in a real environment.

## Operate and recover

- [Quick Start: Deployment Guide](docs/quickstart-deployment.md): Deploying the patterns into a new environment.
- [Deployment Guide: Existing FSx for ONTAP Environment](docs/deployment-guide-existing-fsxn.md): Adding these patterns to an existing FSx for ONTAP file system.
- [Deployment Guide (EN)](docs/en/deployment-guide.md): English deployment walkthrough.
- [ARP Alert Triage Runbook](docs/runbooks/arp-alert-triage.md): First response when an ARP alert fires.
- [Ransomware Recovery Runbook](docs/runbooks/ransomware-recovery.md): Recovering from a ransomware event using snapshots and clones.
- [Scanner Failover Runbook](docs/runbooks/scanner-failover.md): Handling failover of the file-scanning layer.
- [Data Exfiltration Response Runbook](docs/runbooks/data-exfiltration-response.md): First response when bulk reads through SMB, NFS or S3 Access Points are suspected.
- [Operational Considerations (EN)](docs/en/operational-considerations.md): SVM-wide block scope, NTFS name-mapping limits, admin bypass, NACL and NFS caching caveats, data protection and isolated copies.
- [Operational Considerations (JA)](docs/ja/operational-considerations.md): Japanese counterpart with the same sections.
